subtype: Approach: reviewing feedback and adjusting for next time [Revision]
passage: After the talk at the university in Manchester, Daniel found two classmates near the coffee machine. "Can I ask you something? What was unclear?" Mateo thought for a moment. "I liked it. But I only understood what you found when you got to the last slide. Before that I was guessing." The other listener nodded. Daniel felt a small sting, then curiosity. The main result had been sitting in the final minute, behind all the methods. That evening Daniel opened the slides, moved the result to slide three, and marked it with a big number. Next time the talk would start with the answer and then explain how it was reached. Mateo received a message: "Thanks. Very useful."

qa.q: Where in the talk had the main result been?
qa.a: The main result had been in the final minute, on the last slide.

qa.q: What did Daniel feel on hearing that the result came too late?
qa.a: Daniel felt a small sting first and then curiosity, which led to changing the slides.

qa.q: What other approach could help Daniel check the change, and why?
qa.a: Daniel could ask the same two listeners to hear the new order, because they can say if the point arrives earlier.

qa.q: How might Mateo see the talk before the result was moved?
qa.a: Mateo said the listening was like guessing, so the audience was probably lost until the last slide. 🙂

grounding: After a talk, a student asks two listeners what was unclear, learns the result was buried and moves it earlier next time.
